newsitem.title: CHINA: China executes businesswoman in $43 mln fraud.
newsitem.headline: China executes businesswoman in $43 mln fraud.

text.p: China has executed a businesswoman found guilty of defrauding investors in a scam involving as much as 362 million yuan ($43 million), state media said on Friday.

The Supreme People's Court upheld on Wednesday the death sentence against Han Yuji, former president of the Jilin province Yuquan Industrial and Trade Co, for fraud, the China Business Times said. She was executed immediately after sentencing.

In 1986, Han launched a scheme along with her husband Wu Xianquan to raise funds for a private enterprise under her control, offering interest rates of 3.0 percent a month to investors, the newspaper said.

By 1991, Han had raised 362 million yuan in illegal funds but was unable to repay the interest and the managers then destroyed the accounts and the records to prevent detection, it said. A total of 170 billion yuan remained outstanding, the newspaper said.
Han's husband was sentenced to death, with sentence suspended for two years, and the company's vice-president, Jin Yuzi, was jailed for 15 years, it said.

China imposes the death penalty on major cases of corruption and embezzlement to try to halt the spread of graft, which President and Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin has warned is a virus that threatens the survival of the ruling party.
